findings.title: Unreadable Armour Status UI
findings.where: Arena, Road, City screens; right-side CONDITION panel > ARMOUR section
findings.problem: All ARMOUR location statuses use low-contrast dark gray "--" placeholders on a near-black panel, with no visual hierarchy. Sections within CONDITION (ARMOUR, TYRES, PLANT & DRIVER) have no vertical spacing, making the panel cramped and hard to scan.
findings.why: Players cannot quickly assess critical armour status during combat or high-speed travel, and the unreadable text makes the UI look broken/underdeveloped, breaking immersion and removing actionable survival feedback.
findings.fix: Replace "--" with high-contrast white numeric values (or 0% filled progress bars) for each armour location. Add 8px of vertical padding between ARMOUR, TYRES, and PLANT & DRIVER sections to create clear visual hierarchy.

findings.title: City Screen Lack of Visual Differentiation
findings.where: City screen; entire play area (ground, buildings, circular boundary)
findings.problem: The entire ground uses a single uniform cracked concrete texture with no variation. Buildings are tiny, low-detail assets with no function-based visual cues (no unique colors/shapes). The circular boundary is a thin, repetitive line that blends into the ground.
findings.why: Players cannot quickly orient themselves, identify key locations (garages, quest hubs) at a glance, or distinguish the playable area boundary. This slows navigation and makes the open world feel lifeless/underdeveloped.
findings.fix: Add distinct texture/color variations: (1) main roads = dark asphalt with white lane markers, (2) sidewalks = light concrete, (3) parking lots = brown cracked earth. Color-code buildings by function: blue for constructors/garages, yellow for courier pickups, green for shops. Make the circular boundary a 20px thick dark gray wall with a thin yellow inner warning line.

findings.title: Title Screen Tagline & Menu Header Legibility
findings.where: Title screen; below the "SMDUEL" title (tagline) and top of the central menu panel
findings.problem: The tagline ("One car. Sixteen cities. A highway that wants you dead.") is extremely small (~10px), low-contrast light gray on dark background, with no spacing from the title. The menu panel's header text ("$0 | 2030-01-01 (DAY) - smduel") is also small, low-contrast, and blends into the dark panel.
findings.why: Players miss the game's core pitch entirely, and the menu header provides no clear, readable save/context info at a glance, making the title screen feel unpolished and disorganized.
findings.fix: Increase tagline font size to 18px, set color to bright off-white (#f0f0f0), and add 10px top margin from the title. Make menu header text 14px white (#ffffff) with a 2px bright cyan underline (matching the "New Driver" highlight) for cohesion.

findings.title: Constructor Left Panel Visual Hierarchy & Spacing
findings.where: Constructor screen; left-side vehicle parts/stats list
findings.problem: The 10 weapon slots (Weapon 1–10) all display "(empty)" with identical formatting, no vertical spacing, and no indentation. Body stats (Chassis, Suspension, etc.) use the same font weight/color for labels and values, with no spacing between rows.
findings.why: Players cannot quickly scan to select empty weapon slots, and the cramped, uniform formatting makes vehicle customization (a core RPG loop) feel clunky and hard to navigate, slowing down progression.
findings.fix: For weapons: add 4px vertical padding between each row, indent "(empty)" by 12px, and color "(empty)" muted red (#ff6666) to mark unassigned slots. For body stats: make labels (Chassis, etc.) bold white text, values (Light, etc.) regular light gray, with 6px vertical spacing between rows.

findings.title: Non-Functional Radar Panel
findings.where: Arena, Road, City screens; bottom-left RADAR panel
findings.problem: The radar is a static black disc with a tiny central cyan player dot, a static cyan highlight, no contact markers, no sweep animation, and cramped, low-contrast orientation text at the bottom.
findings.why: The radar reads as broken rather than a useful navigation/combat tool, wasting critical screen real estate and removing a key aid for high-speed travel or enemy detection.
findings.fix: Add a rotating 2px thick cyan sweep animation (360-degree rotation every 2 seconds). Add 8x8px color-coded contact markers: orange for enemies, green for objectives, yellow for key locations. Increase orientation text to 14px white (#ffffff), move it to the panel top with 4px padding, and add 1px white 90-degree grid lines to the radar disc.
